overview.intro:
Chapter 37 covers photographic goods that are sensitized or already exposed: **plates and sheet film** (3701) — X-ray film, instant print film, aluminum **printing plates** and photomask blanks — **roll film** (3702), **photographic paper** (3703), exposed film (3704-3706, including developed microfilm and **motion-picture film**) and **photographic chemicals** (3707), a heading CBP uses for photoresists and copier toner. Cameras are chapter 90, and inkjet photo paper, which is not light-sensitive, is chapter 48.

Base rates are low: **22 of 61 lines are Free** and the rest pay 1.4% to 3.7%. The extra duty by country decides the cost. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%** (Japan and Korea 12.5% in total, the EU 10% in total); only exposed film of 3704-3706 can avoid it as **informational materials** (9903.05.92). China pays **25% under Section 301 List 3** on every line. Large printing plates (3701.30) pay **25% Section 232** on full value, and aluminum lithographic printing plates from China and Japan also carry **antidumping duties of 91.83% to 317.43%**. Japan supplied 63% of the $1.57B imported in 2025.

productGroups.label: Photographic plates & sheet film, unexposed (X-ray, instant film, printing plates, photomask blanks)
productGroups.blurb: Unexposed plates and film in the flat: X-ray film (3701.10, 3.7%), instant print film packs (3701.20, 3.7%; Free for Japan under the U.S.-Japan Trade Agreement), plates and film with any side over 255 mm (3701.30, Free — aluminum printing plates, which also pay Section 232) and smaller plates, graphic-arts film and photomask blanks (3701.99, Free). 43% of 2025 imports ($669M).

productGroups.label: Photographic film in rolls, unexposed (35 mm, X-ray, microfilm and motion-picture stock)
productGroups.blurb: Unexposed film in rolls: X-ray film (3702.10), microfilm stock (3702.32.01.30), 35 mm color negative and slide film (3702.53, 3702.54), wide graphic-arts and industrial film (3702.41-3702.44) and motion-picture stock (3702.56). Most lines 3.7%; long 16-35 mm rolls and film over 35 mm wide for color are Free.

productGroups.label: Photographic paper, paperboard & textiles, sensitized, unexposed
productGroups.blurb: Light-sensitive photographic paper, paperboard and textiles, unexposed: silver halide papers (3.7%), other color and black-and-white papers (3.1% or 2.8%), in rolls over 610 mm wide or other sizes. Inkjet photo paper is not sensitized and is classified in chapter 48.

productGroups.label: Plates, film & paper exposed but not developed
productGroups.blurb: Plates, film, paper, paperboard and textiles that have been exposed but not developed — for example exposed rolls sent for processing. Free. Listed by CBP among headings whose goods may qualify as informational materials.

productGroups.label: Plates & film exposed and developed (other than motion-picture film)
productGroups.blurb: Plates and film that have been exposed and developed, other than motion-picture film: developed microfilm and microfiche, slides and transparencies, negatives and other developed plates. Free. 14% of 2025 imports ($221M), led by Taiwan, Germany and Japan.

productGroups.label: Motion-picture film, exposed and developed
productGroups.blurb: Motion-picture film, exposed and developed, with or without a sound track: 35 mm or wider (3706.10) and narrower (3706.90), including positive release prints of feature films. Free, except sound recordings on 35 mm film (3706.10.30, 1.4%).

productGroups.label: Photographic chemicals: emulsions, developers, toners, photoresists
productGroups.blurb: Chemical preparations for photographic uses: sensitizing emulsions (3707.10, 3%) and other preparations and unmixed products put up in measured portions or for retail sale (3707.90, Free) — developers, fixers, color couplers and, per CBP rulings, photoresists and copier toner. 32% of 2025 imports ($496M), 82% from Japan.

workedExamples.title: Aluminum printing plates from Japan
workedExamples.body: Plates with a side over 255 mm are Free at the general rate, but 3701.30.00 is a derivative aluminum article: it pays **25% of full value** under Section 232 (9903.82.09), which replaces Japan's 12.5% Section 301 rate. Aluminum lithographic printing plates are also under an antidumping order: Fujifilm and all other Japanese exporters deposit **91.83%**. On a $100,000 shipment that is $25,000 + $91,830 = **$116,830**.

workedExamples.title: Instant print film from Japan
workedExamples.body: Instant film is 3.7%, Free under the U.S.-Japan Trade Agreement (SPI JP). Japanese goods pay 12.5% in total under the 2026 Section 301 action when the base rate is lower (9903.05.49). Unexposed film is not on CBP's informational-materials list, so a $10,000 shipment pays **$1,250**.

workedExamples.title: 35 mm color film from China
workedExamples.body: 3.7% base + 25% Section 301 List 3 (9903.88.03) + 12.5% 2026 Section 301 (9903.05.31) = **41.2%**: $4,120 on $10,000. No China exclusion covers the line.

workedExamples.title: Developed microfilm from Germany
workedExamples.body: Free at the general rate. EU goods pay 10% in total under the 2026 Section 301 action (9903.05.39), but developed microfilm is informational material: entered under 9903.05.92 it pays **$0**. Without the claim, $1,000 on $10,000.

seo.shortDescription: What changed for photographic film, printing plates, photo paper and photo chemicals (HTS Chapter 37) since January 2025: unchanged base rates, the 2026 Section 301 duties and the informational-materials exemption for exposed film, China's 25% List 3 duty, Section 232 on 3701.30 plates and the AD/CVD orders on aluminum printing plates.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). All 61 Chapter 37 lines carry the **same base rate** in both.

What changed came on top. The 2025 IEEPA tariffs **ended on February 24, 2026**; the Section 122 surcharge that followed expired July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026** the **2026 Section 301 tariffs** charge goods of 60 economies 10% or 12.5% (Japan and Korea 12.5% in total, the EU and Taiwan 10% in total), and Brazil pays a further 25% from July 22. Exposed film of 3704-3706 entered as **informational materials** (9903.05.92) is exempt; unexposed film, paper and chemicals are not. China keeps its **25% List 3** duty on every line. Large plates (**3701.30**) were added to the Section 232 aluminum derivatives list on August 18, 2025 and since **June 8, 2026** pay **25% of full value**. Aluminum lithographic printing plates from China and Japan have been under **antidumping and countervailing duty orders** since November 2024.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 37 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and their informational-materials exemption, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, China Section 301 List 3, Section 232 on derivative aluminum (3701.30), Russia's rates in lieu of column 2 and its 200% aluminum duty, the Nicaragua Section 301 phase-in, the 2025-2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended, and the AD/CVD orders on aluminum lithographic printing plates (explained here, not in the rate grid). No Chapter 37 line is on the Canada Section 338 list or any Section 301 exemption list. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.exemption: Japanese goods pay 12.5% in total in place of a lower base rate (9903.05.49, U.S. note 52(k)); every Chapter 37 line is at or below 3.7%, so 12.5%. changes.title: No Chapter 37 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 61 Chapter 37 lines carry the same general rate in 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition: 22 Free and 39 between 1.4% and 3.7%. No line was added, split or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 continues
changes.detail: USTR received requests to continue the 2018-2019 China Section 301 actions, so they stay in effect during the four-year review. For Chapter 37 this keeps +25% (9903.88.03) on all 61 lines.

No Chapter 37 provision is on any of the lists in Revision 21, so Canadian photographic goods pay only the Section 301 duty, which USMCA goods avoid.

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies, with an informational-materials exemption
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20-9903.05.84), every Chapter 37 line included. EU and Taiwanese goods pay 10% in total and Japanese, Korean and Swiss goods 12.5% in total when the base rate is lower; USMCA-qualifying goods are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94). No Chapter 37 line is on the general exemption list (U.S. note 52(b)) or any country list (52(j)). Heading 9903.05.92 exempts informational materials — for this chapter, exposed film of 3704-3706 — and note 52(f) exempts 3701.30 plates that pay Section 232.

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on all goods of Brazil (9903.05.01), with informational materials exempt (9903.05.09) and goods paying Section 232 excluded (U.S. note 50(a)(vi)). From July 24 the 12.5% 2026 action (9903.05.27) is added on top.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still apply.

changes.title: Section 232: 3701.30 plates listed as derivative aluminum, 25% of full value
changes.detail: Proclamation 11032 revised U.S. note 16 from June 8, 2026 and listed 3701.30.00 in subdivision (c)(vi), derivative aluminum articles. Since then these plates pay 25% of full value (9903.82.09), 15% for UK goods with at least 95% UK aluminum (9903.82.05) and 10% with at least 85% U.S.-smelted aluminum (9903.82.06); none if the aluminum is under 15% of the weight (9903.82.03). changes.title: Printing plates: ITC reconsiders its injury finding on court remand
changes.detail: On February 18, 2026 the Court of International Trade (Slip Op. 26-17, Fujifilm N. Am. Corp. v. United States) sent the ITC's 2024 injury determinations back for it to reconsider whether Fujifilm's U.S. plant is a related party to exclude from the domestic industry. The ITC set its remand procedures; no revocation of the orders has been published, so cash deposits continue.

changes.title: Flexographic photopolymer plates ruled outside the Japan antidumping order
changes.detail: Commerce ruled on November 24, 2025 that Miraclon's flexographic photopolymer printing plates contain no aluminum and are outside the order on aluminum lithographic printing plates from Japan, which covers plates whose substrate is at least 90% aluminum.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. Informational materials (9903.03.11), USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico and Section 232 goods (9903.03.06) were exempt.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil, India and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: First administrative reviews of the printing-plate orders begin
changes.detail: Commerce initiated the first reviews of the antidumping orders on China (A-570-156) and Japan (A-588-881), covering May 1, 2024 to October 31, 2025, and of the China countervailing duty order (C-570-157), covering March 1 to December 31, 2024, for Fujifilm. Until final results are published, the order's cash deposit rates apply.

changes.title: Nicaragua Section 301 tariff phases in from 2027

changes.title: 3701.30 plates added to the Section 232 aluminum derivatives list
changes.detail: Commerce's first inclusions under the derivatives process added 3701.30.0000 to the aluminum list from August 18, 2025: the 50% Section 232 rate (25% for the UK) applied to the aluminum content, and Russian aluminum derivatives paid 200% (9903.85.68). Proclamation 11021 ended the inclusions process on April 6, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Brazil
changes.detail: +40% (9903.01.77) on goods of Brazil, excepting articles covered by 50 U.S.C. 1702(b), including informational materials (9903.01.80). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries — informational materials excepted
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. Section 3(b) excepted articles encompassed by 50 U.S.C. 1702(b): informational materials were entered under 9903.01.31, and CBP named headings 3704, 3705 and 3706 as the Chapter 37 goods that may qualify. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: IEEPA duties on Canada, Mexico and China
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods of Canada (later 35%) and Mexico and +10% (later 20%, then 10%) on goods of China. Each order excluded articles encompassed by 50 U.S.C. 1702(b); CBP set up 9903.01.03, 9903.01.12 and 9903.01.22 for informational materials. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Antidumping and countervailing duty orders on aluminum lithographic printing plates
changes.detail: After the ITC found injury (November 2024), Commerce issued antidumping orders on aluminum lithographic printing plates from China (Fujifilm Printing Plate (China) 115.84%, China-wide 317.43% cash deposit) and Japan (Fujifilm 91.83%, Miraclon 160.11%, all others 91.83%) and a countervailing duty order on China (Fujifilm and all others 35.66%, Shanghai National Ink 229.54%). The scope covers plates with a substrate of at least 90% aluminum, exposed or not, entered under 3701.30.0000 or 3701.99.6060 (also 3701.99.3000 and 8442.50.1000).

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 37 goods were **$1.57B in 2025**, down 1.6% from $1.60B in 2024 and below the 2022 peak of $1.66B. Two groups make up three quarters: **unexposed plates and sheet film (3701), $669M (43%)**, and **photographic chemicals (3707), $496M (32%)** — the heading CBP uses for photoresists and copier toner. Developed plates and film (3705) were $221M (+5%), roll film (3702) fell 22% to $145M and photographic paper (3703) rose 36% to $33M.

**Japan supplied $994M (63%)**, down 4%: $467M of plates and film and $408M of chemicals. **Germany ($153M)** ships mostly plates (3701) and developed film (3705). **Taiwan** (reported to Comtrade as "Other Asia, nes") rose 53% to $97M, three quarters of it developed plates and film (3705). Singapore jumped from $0.9M to $38M, almost all 3701, while Belgium fell 41% and **China fell 66% to $14.5M** — under 1% of the total, after years of the 25% List 3 duty.

The largest 6-digit lines were other chemical preparations (3707.90, $495M), small plates and film including photomask blanks (3701.99, $317M), developed plates and film (3705.00, $221M), large plates such as aluminum printing plates (3701.30, $172M, down 10%) and instant print film (3701.20, $140M). 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data; the 2026 Section 301 and Section 232 changes are not yet in it.

seo.shortDescription: The total U.S. tariff on photographic plates, film, photo paper, developed film and photo chemicals by country: base rate plus the 2026 Section 301 duty, China's 25% List 3 duty and Section 232 on 3701.30 plates, with the informational-materials exemption and USMCA explained.

industryAreas.intro:
Each cell is the **total rate** for the product group from that country: base rate plus extra duties minus preferences, computed from the current tariff schedule with the same engine as the tariff calculator.

Cells for **exposed film** — headings **3704, 3705 and 3706**, such as developed microfilm, slides and motion-picture film — show two totals. **"if yes"** is the rate when the goods are entered as **informational materials** under **9903.05.92** (and 9903.05.09 for Brazil), which removes the 2026 Section 301 duty and Brazil's 25%; **"if no"** is the rate without that claim. These are the only Chapter 37 headings CBP lists as goods that may qualify. Unexposed plates, film and paper (3701-3703) and photographic chemicals (3707) carry no information, so their cells show one total with the Section 301 duty included. The claim never removes **China's 25% List 3** duty.

Plates over 255 mm (**3701.30**, mostly aluminum printing plates) show **25%** from most countries: Section 232 on full value, which replaces the Section 301 duty. AD/CVD duties on aluminum lithographic printing plates from China and Japan are not in the grid; see Tariff updates.

tariffEngineering.h1: Importing Photographic Film, Plates & Chemicals (HTS Ch. 37): Entry Rules, Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Photographic Film, Printing Plates & Photo Chemicals: TSCA, FDA, AD/CVD, Section 232 & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 37) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: How to import Chapter 37 goods: claim 9903.05.92 for exposed film, USMCA and FTA claims, Chapter 98 provisions for educational films and U.S. film exposed abroad, metal-content headings for 3701.30 plates, AD/CVD scope — plus TSCA, FDA, hazmat and marking rules.

tariffEngineering.intro:
Base rates in Chapter 37 are small; the extra duties are not. The levers that matter: enter **exposed film** (3704-3706) as **informational materials** under 9903.05.92; claim **USMCA** or another FTA where the goods qualify; use a **Chapter 98** provision for educational films, film for libraries and religious institutions, or U.S. film exposed abroad; for **3701.30** plates, document the **metal content**, since plates without aluminum or under 15% aluminum by weight pay no Section 232 duty; and check whether a plate falls inside the **AD/CVD orders** on aluminum lithographic printing plates from China and Japan.

Entry rules: photographic chemicals need a **TSCA certification** and often **hazmat** shipping papers; medical **X-ray film** is an FDA device whose foreign maker must be registered; every article must be **marked** with its country of origin; and CBP can detain **piratical copies** of copyrighted films and seize obscene matter.

levers.title: Enter exposed film as informational materials under 9903.05.92 (and 9903.05.09 for Brazil)
levers.saves: The whole 10%-12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty, and for Brazil the 25% Brazil duty too
levers.appliesTo: Exposed film of headings 3704, 3705 and 3706 — developed microfilm and microfiche, slides, negatives, motion-picture film — from any of the 60 economies or Brazil
levers.document: Report 9903.05.92 (and 9903.05.09 for Brazil) on the entry line with the Chapter 37 number, and keep a description showing the film carries images, text or sound.
levers.caveat: Not for unexposed film, plates, paper or chemicals (3701-3703, 3707), which CBP's list does not name. It does not lift China's 25% List 3 duty, Russia's rates or the Nicaragua duty from 2027. CBP decides whether goods are informational materials; a heading on its list means goods may qualify, not that every product does.

levers.title: Claim USMCA on film, plates and chemicals made in Canada or Mexico
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty for Canada or Mexico, and the base rate (up to 3.7%)
levers.appliesTo: All 61 lines. 3701-3703: a change from any heading outside 3701-3703, so coating film base or paper in Canada or Mexico qualifies but slitting or cutting imported jumbo rolls does not; 3704-3706: a change from any other heading; 3707: a change of subheading, or a chemical reaction in a USMCA country
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, in any format, with the information listed in 19 CFR 182.12.
levers.caveat: USMCA does not remove the 25% Section 232 duty on 3701.30 plates (U.S. note 16(b)). The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

levers.title: Claim the FTA rate on 3.7%, 3.1%, 2.8%, 3% and 1.4% lines
levers.saves: The base rate (up to 3.7%) for FTA partners whose Section 301 duty is added on top of it, such as Singapore, Australia, Chile, Colombia, Israel, Morocco and Peru
levers.appliesTo: The 39 dutiable lines (3701.10, 3701.20, 3701.91, most of 3702 and 3703, 3706.10.30, 3707.10); instant print film (3701.20) is also Free for Japan (SPI JP)
levers.document: The SPI on the entry line and the origin records each agreement requires (19 CFR part 10 and part 182).
levers.caveat: For Japan, South Korea, the EU, Taiwan and Switzerland the Section 301 rate is a total that replaces a lower base rate, so an FTA claim does not lower what they pay unless the goods are also informational materials. GSP has been expired since December 31, 2020.

levers.title: Use a Chapter 98 provision where the film or the importer qualifies
levers.saves: The base rate and the 2026 Section 301 and Brazil duties, which do not apply to goods properly entered under Chapter 98 (other than 9802.00.40-.60 and 9802.00.80)
levers.appliesTo: Exposed and developed film, microfilm and slides for education, libraries, religious institutions and government; U.S.-made film exposed abroad; U.S. goods returned
levers.document: The Chapter 98 number on the entry line, plus what the provision requires — for 9817.00.40-.44 a U.S. Department of State certificate that the materials are educational, scientific or cultural (19 CFR 10.121).
levers.caveat: Each provision has conditions and CBP must agree the entry is appropriate. Chapter 98 entries still owe Section 232 duty on 3701.30 (U.S. note 16(b)) and any AD/CVD.

levers.title: Document the metal content of 3701.30 plates
levers.saves: The 25% Section 232 duty — none for plates without aluminum, steel or copper (9903.82.01) or with metal under 15% of the weight (9903.82.03); 10% instead of 25% with at least 85% U.S.-smelted aluminum (9903.82.06)
levers.appliesTo: 3701.30.00.00 only: photopolymer, polyester or other non-aluminum plates and film over 255 mm, and plates made with U.S. aluminum
levers.document: Report the 9903.82 heading that fits and the metal content information CBP requires; keep mill or supplier records of the aluminum's weight share and where it was smelted and cast.
levers.caveat: Plates up to 255 mm (3701.99) are not on the Section 232 list at all. Aluminum lithographic plates are at least 90% aluminum, so they pay 25%. Without the 232 duty, the 2026 Section 301 duty applies instead.

levers.title: Check the AD/CVD scope before buying plates from China or Japan
levers.saves: Antidumping deposits of 91.83%-317.43% and countervailing deposits of 35.66%-229.54%
levers.appliesTo: Printing plates of 3701.30, 3701.99.30 and 3701.99.60.60 from China or Japan; plates whose substrate is not aluminum (rubber, plastic, photopolymer) are excluded from the orders
levers.document: A scope ruling request to Commerce (19 CFR 351.225) when it is unclear; the substrate specification for the entry file.
levers.caveat: The written scope decides, not the HTS number. Commerce ruled on November 24, 2025 that Miraclon's flexographic photopolymer plates are outside the Japan order. Plates coated in China or Japan and cut or imaged in a third country stay in scope.

levers.title: Get a binding ruling where the line decides the duty
levers.saves: Section 232 (3701.30 vs 3701.99), the AD/CVD scope, or a wrong chapter altogether
levers.appliesTo: Plates near the 255 mm boundary, photomask blanks (3701.99.60.60), photoresists and toner (3707.90.32), and papers that are not sensitized (inkjet photo paper is chapter 48)
levers.document: A ruling request to CBP with a sample or full description (19 CFR 177.2).
levers.caveat: Classification follows the goods, not the duty: a plate with any side over 255 mm is 3701.30 whatever its use.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about importing photographic film, plates, paper and chemicals into the U.S. — HS codes, tariffs by country and entry rules. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: Chapter 37 base rates are low and unchanged since January 2025: 22 of 61 lines Free, the rest 1.4%-3.7%.

Since July 24, 2026 the 2026 Section 301 duty (10% or 12.5%; 12.5% in total for Japan) applies to nearly every line; only exposed film of 3704-3706 can be entered duty-free of it as informational materials (9903.05.92).
China pays 25% Section 301 List 3 on all 61 lines plus the 12.5% 2026 duty — and its share of U.S. imports fell to under 1% in 2025.
Plates over 255 mm (3701.30) pay 25% Section 232 on full value since June 8, 2026, and aluminum lithographic printing plates from China and Japan carry AD/CVD deposits of 35.66% to 317.43%.
Photographic chemicals (3707), including photoresists and toner, need a TSCA certification; medical X-ray film needs FDA device registration.

faqs.question: What does HTS Chapter 37 cover?
faqs.answer: Photographic and cinematographic goods that are light-sensitive or already exposed: plates and sheet film (3701), roll film (3702), photographic paper (3703), exposed but undeveloped film (3704), developed plates and film such as microfilm (3705), motion-picture film (3706) and photographic chemicals (3707). It has 61 tariff lines; 22 are Free and the rest pay 1.4% to 3.7%. Cameras are chapter 90.

faqs.question: What is HS code 3701 and 3701.30?
faqs.answer: Heading 3701 is unexposed photographic plates and film in the flat: 3701.10 X-ray film (3.7%), 3701.20 instant print film (3.7%), 3701.30 plates and film with any side over 255 mm (Free) and 3701.91/3701.99 smaller color and other plates (3.7% or Free). 3701.30 holds most aluminum printing plates; since June 8, 2026 it pays 25% Section 232 on full value from most countries.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for camera film and 35 mm film?
faqs.answer: Unexposed roll film is heading 3702. 35 mm color negative film in rolls up to 30 m is 3702.54.00.30, 35 mm color slide film 3702.53.00.30, and black-and-white film up to 35 mm and 30 m 3702.96.00.00 — all 3.7%. Exposed film is 3704 and developed film 3705. Film cameras are not chapter 37; they are classified in heading 9006.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and tariff for Polaroid and Instax instant film?
faqs.answer: Instant print film in packs is 3701.20 (3.7%; color 3701.20.00.30). Unexposed film is not informational material, so the 2026 Section 301 duty applies: 12.5% in total from Japan (Free base under the U.S.-Japan agreement), 10% in total from the EU, 41.2% from China (3.7% + 25% + 12.5%) and 3.7% from countries outside the 60 economies.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for X-ray film?
searchedAs: hs code for x ray film
faqs.answer: X-ray film in the flat is 3701.10 and in rolls 3702.10, both 3.7%; medical film other than dental is statistical suffix .30. Medical X-ray film is a Class I FDA device (21 CFR 892.1840), so the foreign manufacturer must register and list it with FDA. X-ray film viewers are not chapter 37.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for printing plates?
searchedAs: hs code for photopolymer printing plates
hs code for flexographic printing plate
faqs.answer: Light-sensitive printing plates are heading 3701: 3701.30.00.00 when any side exceeds 255 mm and 3701.99.60.60 when smaller, both Free. CBP has classified aluminum imagesetter plates in 3701.30 and photopolymer plate material in 3701.99.60. Plates that are not light-sensitive, such as plates prepared for printing under heading 8442, fall outside chapter 37.

faqs.question: Are there antidumping duties on aluminum lithographic printing plates?
faqs.answer: Yes, since November 22, 2024. Antidumping deposits are 91.83% for Fujifilm and other Japanese exporters (160.11% Miraclon), 115.84% for Fujifilm Printing Plate (China) and 317.43% for other Chinese exporters; Chinese plates also owe countervailing duty of 35.66% (229.54% Shanghai National Ink). The ITC is reconsidering its injury finding on a 2026 court remand; no revocation has been published, so deposits continue. Section 232 adds 25% on 3701.30 plates.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for photo paper?
faqs.answer: Light-sensitive (silver halide) photographic paper is heading 3703: 3.7% for silver halide papers and 3.1% or 2.8% for others. Inkjet photo paper is not sensitized, so it is not chapter 37: CBP classified glossy and satin inkjet photo papers in heading 4810 (ruling N017451).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for toner powder?
faqs.answer: CBP classifies copier toner powder in 3707.90.32.90, a Free line (ruling N019393); photoresists are in the same line (HQ W967818). Toner cartridges are printer parts of heading 8443. From Japan, toner pays 12.5% in total under the 2026 Section 301 action; from China 37.5%. Chemical toner entries need a TSCA certification.

faqs.question: What does HS code 3707.90 cover?
faqs.answer: Chemical preparations for photographic uses other than sensitizing emulsions (3707.10, 3%), and unmixed products put up in measured portions or for retail sale: acid violet 19 (3707.90.31), other preparations such as developers, fixers, color couplers, photoresists and toner (3707.90.32) and unmixed products (3707.90.60). All Free. 3707.90 was $495M of 2025 imports, the chapter's largest line.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for microfilm?
faqs.answer: Developed microfilm and microfiche are 3705.00.00.00 (Free); unexposed microfilm stock is 3702.32.01.30 (3.7%). Developed microfilm can be entered as informational material under 9903.05.92, removing the 2026 Section 301 duty, and microfilm certified as educational can enter under 9817.00.42.

faqs.question: What is the informational materials exemption from tariffs?
faqs.answer: IEEPA bars regulating imports of informational materials (50 U.S.C. 1702(b)(3)), so the 2025 IEEPA tariffs excluded them, and the 2026 Section 301 and Brazil actions repeat the exemption (9903.05.92, 9903.05.09). In Chapter 37 CBP lists headings 3704, 3705 and 3706 — exposed film — as goods that may qualify; blank film, plates, paper and chemicals do not. China's 25% List 3 duty has no such exemption.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on films made outside the U.S.?
searchedAs: tariffs on films made outside us
tariffs on movies made outside us
faqs.answer: As of October 13, 2026 no tariff heading targets motion pictures: the 2026 Revision 21 schedule has no Chapter 99 duty on films as such. Exposed motion-picture film (3706) is Free, or 1.4% for 35 mm sound recordings, and as informational material it can be entered under 9903.05.92 free of the 2026 Section 301 duty. China's 25% List 3 duty still applies.
